sentences.text: Following seas are especially dangerous for small powerboats.
A broach happens when a wave from astern lifts the stern and slews the boat sideways, where the next wave can roll it.
In extreme cases a boat can pitchpole, with the bow burying and the stern flipping over the top.
When running before big seas or entering an inlet, ride on the back of a wave, matching its speed, rather than surfing down its face.
Raise the trim tabs to keep the bow up, and be ready with the throttle.
